title: Apollo Research wants AI evaluators inside the lab during training, not just at launch
key_facts: AI safety group Apollo Research argues independent evaluators should have continuous access to models during training, calling it 'embedded evaluations'.
It published its case in blog posts between 30 Sep and 5 Oct 2026.
Today, external evaluations usually happen shortly before a public release; Apollo says the most informative moments have passed by then.
The aim is to catch behaviours such as scheming while they form; Apollo wants close to employee-level access.
Apollo CEO Marius Hobbhahn testified in early October 2026 before a US Senate Homeland Security subcommittee, advocating mandatory independent evaluations.
Apollo, founded in 2023, focuses on deceptive alignment, where a system appears well-behaved while pursuing other goals.
Crypto Briefing notes labs would have to share far more than they do now.
quote_evidence: The group argues that independent evaluators should have continuous access to AI models throughout training, not just a brief look right before a public release.
Apollo laid out its case in a series of blog posts published between September 30 and October 5, 2026.
Hobbhahn advocated for mandatory independent evaluations in AI development.
why_it_matters_hint: Access to training is the sticking point for independent AI safety testing.
notes: Apollo's blog posts began before 6 Oct but the story was reported 6 Oct; score kept. No lab has agreed to the proposal in the text. Crypto Briefing is a secondary outlet summarising Apollo's posts.
